On each circle, the half-turn sends the distance s to ell/2−s, including s=0 and s=ell/2. Summing proves ρ(τx,a)=D−ρ(x,a). Substituting y=τx converts the maximum of the nearer distances to D minus the minimum of the farther distances, with a,b unchanged. In the latter problem, the triangle inequality gives lower bound ρ(a,b)/2, and a product of shortest-arc midpoints attains it simultaneously in every coordinate, including ties and coincident sites. Applying τ to this midpoint recovers the frozen proof's longer-arc witness. Maximizing ρ(a,b) is exactly saturating each coordinate's cap ell_j/2; this proves the antipodal rigidity and subtracting D/2 proves the excess formula. This checks all dimensions and cases without sampling. value.rationale: The facility problem is natural and the formula correct, but the proposed new contribution adds no nonmechanical exact fact: half-turn complementation is immediate coordinate by coordinate and simply rewrites the quantity as D minus the textbook enclosing radius of a two-point set in a geodesic space. That enclosing radius is forced by the triangle inequality and attained at any shortest-path midpoint. Once this equivalence is written down, no product-torus optimization, exceptional aspect or boundary regime remains to classify. Saturation of each coordinate gives rigidity and subtraction gives the excess formula verbatim from that automatic identity. The asserted useful comparison of arbitrary sites is exactly this routine deduction, not a further geometric constraint or outcome. Reject on that scientific basis, not on an access failure or on proof length alone. There is no independently valuable remainder in the frozen claim that can be rescued by narrower wording.
